items.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013
items.q: Like Dizzy Gillespie sounded like Roy Eldridge in those early years.

ctx.x: Well you know you have to sound like someone in order to sound like yourself. In the beginning of, in the formative years of your being able to play at an advanced skill level in improvisation, you’d want to sound like somebody else. Like Dizzy Gillespie sounded like Roy Eldridge in those early years. Miles Davis sounded like Dizzy in his early years. And Lee Morgan sounded like Clifford Brown in his early years you know. So when they eventually got tired of playing that way they started going into their own…
Well said. I’m just going to take a crack and run a few names by you. Joe Wilder?
